title: Babel
events_chronological: In Tokyo the deaf teenager Chieko Wataya is the one who finds her mother dead after she takes her own life.
On a hunting trip in Morocco the Japanese businessman Yasujiro Wataya makes a gift of his rifle to his guide Hassan.
Hassan sells the rifle on to the goatherd Abdullah, who needs it for the jackals taking his flock.
Abdullah hands the rifle to his sons Ahmed and Yussef and sends them into the hills with the goats.
The boys argue about how far the rifle will carry, and Yussef fires at a distant tourist bus to settle it.
American tourists Richard and Susan Jones, travelling to repair a marriage broken by the cot death of their baby, are on that bus.
The bullet goes through Susan's shoulder and the bus turns off for the village of Tazarine.
Richard begs the embassy for a helicopter while a village vet stitches Susan and the other tourists grow mutinous and drive away.
In San Diego the Joneses' nanny Amelia, unable to find anyone to cover for her, takes Mike and Debbie across the border to her son's wedding.
Chieko is humiliated at a volleyball match and then brushed off by boys in a restaurant because she cannot speak.
Chieko takes off her underwear at the table and later exposes herself to her dentist, hunting for any reaction at all.
Moroccan police trace the rifle back to Hassan and beat his family until he names Abdullah.
A helicopter finally lifts Susan out to a hospital in Casablanca.
Amelia's nephew Santiago drives the children back drunk, panics at the border checkpoint and abandons the three of them in the desert.
Amelia walks into the desert with the children, leaves them under a tree to find help, and is arrested by the border patrol.
Police corner Abdullah's family in the rocks; Ahmed is shot dead and Yussef surrenders, confessing that he fired the shot.
Amelia is deported to Mexico after sixteen years in the United States, though the children are found alive.
Detective Kenji tells Chieko that the police only wanted to confirm what became of the rifle her father legally gave away.
Chieko meets Kenji naked at her door, then weeps in his arms and hands him a folded note.
Yasujiro comes home and holds his daughter on the balcony high above Tokyo.
syuzhet_notes: The four strands are intercut without captions and are not simultaneous: the Tokyo material - told-order bullets 7, 9, 10 and 17-20 - runs days after the Moroccan shooting, even though it is cut in as if concurrent. The two events that set the rifle in motion, Yasujiro's gift and the death of Chieko's mother, are held back as late revelations at told-order bullets 18 and 10 despite being the earliest things in the story.
fabula_notes: The death of the Joneses' baby, which is why they are in Morocco at all, exists only in a line of dialogue. The interval between Yasujiro's hunting trip and Hassan's sale of the rifle is never stated, and the children's rescue in the desert happens off screen and is reported to Amelia after the fact.
